Anvil Browser

The Anvil Browser is a high-performance desktop web browser engineered with clean-room architecture. It features multi-engine execution integrating the Prism CSS engine, the Cinder JavaScript runtime, and standalone pure-Go components for typography and image codecs[1].

Anvil Browser
Initial release 2026
Original author Buntato
CSS Engine Prism
JS Engine Cinder
Font Engine Anvil-TTF (Pure Go)
Image Engine Anvil-Image (Pure Go)

History

Development commenced with a mandate for strict modularity, high memory safety, and verifiable independent subsystems. The architecture isolates web layout, script execution, network transport, and surface compositing into decoupled modules.

Architecture

The rendering pipeline processes documents through strict sequential stages:

  • HTML Parsing: Transforms character streams into balanced DOM node trees.
  • Style Resolution: Evaluates Selectors Level 4 and computes cascaded property bags.
  • Layout Computation: Places block, inline, and table boxes onto a geometric Cartesian plane.
  • DisplayList Recording: Emits structured 2D drawing primitives.

Core Subsystems

Subsystem Role Language Key Capabilities
Prism CSS Styling C++20 & Rust Selectors Level 4, CSS variables, @media queries, color math
Cinder Script Execution C++20, Rust & JS NaN-boxed VM, polymorphic inline caches, DOM/Web APIs
Anvil-TTF Font Engine Pure Go SFNT tables, TrueType outlines, subpixel phase hinting
Anvil-Image Image Codecs Pure Go PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP (lossy/lossless), ICO, BMP

Performance Metrics

Subsystem benchmarks demonstrate low-overhead execution across complex responsive layouts and intensive DOM operations.
